observed_ui_rules.statement: A refund can only be requested once per order; after a refund request is created, the "Request refund" action becomes unavailable and refund.status moves from none to pending.

inference.text: The workflow intends a refund to be requestable only once per order; the server should reject a second /api/order/refund/request call while a refund is already pending or completed.

observed_ui_rules.statement: The "Complete refund" action is available only while a refund is pending, and disappears permanently once the refund is completed (terminal, one-time completion).

inference.text: The workflow intends refund completion to occur exactly once; the server should reject a repeat /api/order/refund/complete call, and should reject the call entirely if no refund was ever requested (skip-step).

observed_ui_rules.statement: Price protection adjustment is presented as unavailable while another order request (a refund) is active.

facts.text: paragraph : Price protection is not available while another order request is active.

inference.text: The workflow intends price-protection adjustments and refund requests to be mutually exclusive per order; no price-adjustment endpoint was recorded in this session to test server-side enforcement directly.

observed_ui_rules.statement: Once an order is canceled, the Cancel order and Request refund controls disappear and are no longer available.

inference.text: The order-cancellation workflow intends the cancel and refund-request actions to become permanently unavailable once cancellation completes.

observed_ui_rules.statement: Price protection becomes unavailable to the customer while another order request (cancellation) is active.

facts.text: paragraph : The price of this item has dropped since your purchase.
paragraph : Price protection is not available while another order request is active.

inference.text: The client displays price protection as 'Unavailable' once cancellation is active, even though the server-side priceProtection.status field is not observed to change (remains 'eligible' in both GET /api/order and POST /api/order/cancel responses). This is an unverified hypothesis worth testing server-side: the API may still accept a price-adjustment request after cancellation despite the UI hiding the control.

observed_ui_rules.statement: Price adjustment can only be requested once — the control becomes unavailable immediately after it is issued

inference.text: The UI treats price adjustment as single-use once issued; the server should independently reject a second price-adjustment request for the same order rather than relying on the client to hide the button.

observed_ui_rules.statement: Cancelling the order becomes unavailable once a price adjustment has been issued

inference.text: The client disables cancellation client-side after a price adjustment is issued; the server should also reject a cancel-order call in this state rather than trusting the UI gate.
